description: crypto/aes (Go stdlib, frozen copy): the FIPS-140 module reorganization moved the real implementation to internal/fips140/aes, dwarfing the rest of the module (6426 of 7746 mutants live there alone -- see PROPOSAL.md's Evidence section for the layer-story writeup this fixture backs). Captured directly against the built binary, package scope, default operator set, -mutatetimeout=30s. This module was checked via commit archaeology as far as a spot-check went before being deprioritized; not confirmed as an exact upstream commit pin the way stdlib-strconv-parseuint is. killed/survived were corrected from an original 5211/2305 to 5210/2306 after two independent TestCorpus re-verifications reproducibly disagreed with the original capture on exactly one mutant (internal/fips140/aes/aes_generic.go:112, operator/binary ^->&) -- investigated and root-caused: the original capture's single run hit the fixed 30s -mutatetimeout on that mutant under -mutateparallel=10 CPU contention, and classify() correctly counted the timeout as Killed; every other observed run (including this correction) finds that mutant's go test completes in well under a second and Survives cleanly. Not a turango bug -- a one-off scheduling blip against a fixed per-mutant timeout during the original capture.
